claims.text: The Co-free FeNiCrMn alloy is considered in a solidified solid-solution state.
The alloy's temperature- and strain-rate-dependent dynamic behavior is governed by an interaction between dislocation glide and deformation twinning.
The balance between dislocation glide and twinning is influenced by the alloy's chemical composition and crystal structure.
Dislocation density and twin-boundary formation are the structural mediators of the proposed dynamic behavior.
The proposed mechanism is applicable from 20°C to 500°C and from 10^-3 s^-1 to 10^3 s^-1.
At room temperature and 10^-3 s^-1, Co-free FeNiCrMn will have 20% higher yield strength than equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi.
At room temperature and 10^-3 s^-1, Co-free FeNiCrMn will have 15% higher ductility than equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi.

Matched tensile tests and molecular-dynamics simulations across the specified temperature and strain-rate ranges can evaluate yield strength, ductility, dislocation density, and twin-boundary formation.
The relative contributions of dislocation glide and twinning may vary with testing conditions.
The hypothesis is falsified if, at room temperature and 10^-3 s^-1, yield strength and ductility do not exceed the equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi baseline by at least 15% and 10%, respectively.

contradictions.description: The prediction specifies 20% higher yield strength and 15% higher ductility, whereas the falsification rule only requires increases of 15% and 10%. Results below the stated prediction could therefore fail to falsify the hypothesis.
